explanation: RAII is a fundamental C++ programming technique that ensures resources (memory, files, network connections, etc.) are automatically managed.  It ties resource allocation to the lifetime of an object. When the object goes out of scope, its destructor is called, automatically releasing the resource. This prevents resource leaks and simplifies error handling. Smart pointers are crucial for implementing RAII effectively. They act as proxies for raw pointers, automatically managing the lifetime of the dynamically allocated objects they point to.
